draft.title: Levels of biodiversity
card: Biodiversity is the variety of life. Geographers look at it at three levels: genes, species and ecosystems.
Genetic diversity
the variety of genes within one species. A population with many gene variations is more likely to include individuals that can cope with a disease or a change in climate.
Species diversity
the variety of different species in an area. It counts how many species there are and how evenly numbers are spread among them.
Ecosystem diversity
the variety of habitats and ecosystems in a region, such as forest, wetland, grassland and reef.
draft.remember: Biodiversity is variety within a species, between species and between ecosystems.

a.q: A region has rainforest, mangroves, heath and coral reef. Which level of biodiversity does this describe?
opts: Ecosystem diversity
Species diversity
Genetic diversity
Population density
a.why: The region contains many different types of ecosystem, so this is ecosystem diversity. It is not species diversity, because that counts the different species rather than the types of habitat.
a.clue: Look at what is being counted: habitats, species or genes?

b.q: Koalas in one park all descend from a few animals and have very similar genes. Which level of biodiversity is low, and why does it matter?
opts: Genetic, so few may cope with a new disease
Species, so few other animals can live in the park
Ecosystem, so few habitat types are in the park
Genetic, so the park must have too many koalas
b.why: The problem is the small variety of genes within one species, which is low genetic diversity. With similar genes, few koalas may resist a new disease. Species diversity is the wrong level, because the case is about one species only.
b.clue: The case is about variety inside a single species.

b.best: Genetic, so few may cope with a new disease

problems.detail: The distractor 'Genetic, so the park must have too many koalas' uses 'must', an absolute word the card does not use. It lets a student rule it out on wording alone rather than understanding.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate, and the intended answers are clearly right. The only issue is one distractor in question b that uses 'must', which makes it easy to dismiss on wording alone.
